name: Vessel
description: Plays the sound inside a body that rings: a bottle, a pipe, a shell, a drum or a soundboard, of any size and material.

params.name: Body
params.description: The thing the sound is put inside. A bottle has one deep note, a pipe an even ladder of them, a shell a high cluster, a drum and a soundboard uneven ones.

params.name: Size
params.description: How big the body is. Larger moves every resonance down together, from a thimble to a cistern, and the pitch of what is ringing glides with it.

params.name: Material
params.description: How long the body rings once struck. Low is clay and damp wood that only colour the sound; high is glass and metal that sing on after it.

params.name: Opening
params.description: How much of the inside gets out. Closed is boxy, mostly the low resonances; open lets the upper ones out and more of the sound itself through.

params.name: Air
params.description: The body's own breath: a hiss blown through the same resonances, rising and falling with what you play and silent when you stop.

params.name: Tone
params.description: Tilts what comes out of the body. Low is darker, high is brighter, and the middle leaves it as the body made it.

params.name: Width
params.description: How far apart the two ears are inside the body. At zero both sides hear the same; higher, each side favours different resonances. Deep ones stay in the middle.

params.name: Mix
params.description: The balance between the sound as it was and the sound from inside the body.

params.name: Position
params.description: Where in the body the sound is heard. Each resonance is strong in some places and absent in others; only a bottle's deep note is the same everywhere.

origin.note: A bank of sixteen two-pole resonances per side beside a share of the sound itself. The pipes' series and the drum's ratios are the textbook ones; the shell, the soundboard and every strength are made by hand; see bodies.h.
